title: NO SUCH THING as "EXTENDED" WARRANTY - Kevin Hunter The Homework Guy
summary: The Homework Guy and a co-host argue that a paid third-party 'extended warranty' is not legally a warranty, pays out little, and is sometimes illegally tied to financing.

assertions.quote: it can only be legally called a warranty if it comes from the manufacturer and is included in the price

verdicts.note: Matches the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act's definition, though dealers often blur the terms in marketing anyway.

FTC states an auto service contract/extended warranty "is not a warranty as defined by federal law, because you buy it separately; it's not included when you buy a car" -- matching the legal distinction the claim draws.

assertions.quote: they pay just 10 to 12 cents per dollar spent on them
up to 70% markups in many cases
that's called tying the sale and it violates the Truth and Lending Act

verdicts.note: Matches FTC's 'implied tying' enforcement actions against dealers for bundling warranties with financing.

assertions.quote: You'll pay half the price with clearer terms

verdicts.note: Consistent with reported dealer markups, though the exact discount varies by provider and region.

NCLC found a credit union sold GAP directly at a flat $275 versus the dataset's dealer-sold GAP averaging $629-$655 (about 42-44% of the dealer price, roughly in the "about half" range the claim describes) -- but this comparison is for GAP, not vehicle service contracts.
